message.content:
In the key of **A** the blues scale follows the classic “minor‑blues” pattern:

| Scale degree | Interval from the root | Note (in A) |
|--------------|------------------------|-------------|
| 1 (root)     | 0 semitones            | A           |
| b3 (minor 3rd)| +3 semitones          | C           |
| 4 (perfect 4th)| +5 semitones         | D           |
| b5 (diminished 5th / augmented 4th)| +6 semitones | Eb |
| 5 (perfect 5th)| +7 semitones          | E           |
| b7 (minor 7th)| +10 semitones         | G           |
| 8 (octave)   | +12 semitones          | A           |

So the A blues scale is: **A – C – D – Eb – E – G – A**.

(If you prefer the interval pattern: 1, b3, 4, b5, 5, b7, 8.)
